बॉलीवुड में एक्टिंग का सपना देखना जितना आसान है, रोल पाना उतना ही मुश्किल! 🎬

Goa में आयोजित 57th IFFI के मास्टरक्लास में कास्टिंग डायरेक्टर Mukesh Chhabra ने अपनी जर्नी के कई हैरान करने वाले खुलासे किए।

Mukesh Chhabra ने बताया कि फिल्म Dangal के लिए लगभग 14,000 लड़कियों के ऑडिशन लिए गए थे और इसमें 2 साल का लंबा समय लगा था! 😲

इसके अलावा आने वाली फिल्म Ramayana की कास्टिंग प्रक्रिया 6 साल तक चली, जबकि Gangs of Wasseypur के लिए उन्होंने 384 लोगों को कास्ट किया था।

इंडस्ट्री में 20 से ज्यादा साल पूरे कर चुके छाबड़ा ने बताया कि Aamir Khan उन शुरुआती लोगों में थे जिन्होंने उनके काम को पहचाना था और अब अगले 2-3 सालों में उनके पास 100 फिल्में हैं।

नए एक्टर्स को सलाह देते हुए उन्होंने कहा कि self-tapes में साफ बैकग्राउंड, सही लाइटिंग और किरदार की समझ बहुत जरूरी है। 💡

इतनी बड़ी फिल्मों की कास्टिंग में लगने वाले इस लंबे समय पर आपकी क्या राय है? कमेंट में जरूर बताएं! 👇

ctx.title: Around 14,000 girls auditioned for the roles: Mukesh Chhabra recalls casting of Dangal at IFFI 2026
ctx.summary: Mukesh Chhabra, the casting director behind 'Dangal' and Shah Rukh Khan's upcoming 'King,' took aspiring actors and filmmakers behind the scenes.
ctx.text:
Panjim (Goa) [India], November 27 (ANI): Mukesh Chhabra, the casting director behind 'Dangal' and Shah Rukh Khan's upcoming 'King,' took aspiring actors and filmmakers behind the scenes of the casting process at a masterclass at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.
The session, “The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged," turned into an extended conversation, with participants asking about everything from self-tapes and social media to age and the demands of the profession, reported Variety.
At the session, Chhabra recalled the casting of Dangal, Chhabra revealed that it took nearly two years, with around 14,000 girls auditioning for the roles.
"It took nearly two years, with around 14,000 girls auditioning for the roles. The casting process for Ramayana extended over six years," he said. He also recalled casting 384 people for Gangs of Wasseypur, a film that proved to be a major turning point in his career. "Gangs of Wasseypur changed my life", he said, as quoted in a press release shared by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
Reflecting on his journey of over two decades, Chhabra spoke about how actor Aamir Khan was among the first people to notice his work. He said that his journey has been driven by an enduring passion for discovering new talent. With around 100 more films lined up over the next two to three years, he said he remains deeply invested in the process.
“There is so much talent in our country. I send my team all over the country to scout for talent. You have to go to the roots. Our country has so many cultural arts and sub-cultures where so much raw talent is displayed.” Directors, he added, hire him for his "opinion, ideas, not for data,” as quoted in a press note.
At the session, Chhabra urged actors preparing for an audition to go beyond memorising lines and analyse a character’s background, circumstances, social position and motivations.
“Designing the scene in your head is important. We want to understand the actor’s intellect. Please do your homework. If you understand life, you can understand acting,” said Chhabra as quoted in a press note.
On self-tapes, his advice was to choose a clean background, ensure good lighting and clear sound, use someone who can deliver cues naturally, and frame the shot close enough to capture the face and eyes.
“I want to focus on your face, your performance, not on the painting behind you,” he said as quoted in a press note.
Chhabra casting credits include 'Dhurandhar,' Aamir Khan’s 'Dangal,' Anurag Kashyap’s 'Gangs of Wasseypur,' Nitesh Tiwari’s 'Ramayana' and 'King,' due December 24. (ANI)
